title: The History of Mario Kart | From Super Mario Kart To Mario Kart World | Gaming History
description: The history of Mario Kart: Super Mario Kart in 1992, every major console game, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe in 2017 and Mario Kart World, the Nintendo Switch 2 launch game from June 2025.

sections.heading: The racing game everyone plays
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are going through the history of Mario Kart, the racing series where a lucky shell at the last corner can change everything. It is one of Nintendo's most popular series, a favourite at parties and family get togethers, and it has been around for more than three decades. Along the way it has moved from the Super Nintendo to handhelds, home consoles and phones, and the numbers behind it are huge, so there is plenty to cover. We will begin with Super Mario Kart in nineteen ninety two, walk through the big console games, look at how Mario Kart Eight Deluxe became the biggest seller of all, and finish with Mario Kart World, the racing game that launched with the Nintendo Switch two in June twenty twenty five. Every date comes from Wikipedia and from news and record pages. Let us get to the start line.

sections.heading: Super Mario Kart
sections.script: The series began with Super Mario Kart for the Super Nintendo, which was released in nineteen ninety two, first in Japan in August and then in other regions. It was a racing game with Mario characters, the first one in what became a very long line, played from above with a special pseudo three dimensional look, and it let two players race side by side with a split screen. Its racing was fast, but the real fun came from the items, which you could throw at rivals to slow them down. According to Guinness World Records, Super Mario Kart sold eight point seven six million copies worldwide and is listed as the best selling racing game on the SNES. This one game set the pattern that every sequel has followed.

sections.heading: Mario Kart 64 and Double Dash
sections.script: The second game, Mario Kart sixty four, arrived on the Nintendo sixty four, with a first release in Japan in December nineteen ninety six. It brought real three dimensional tracks and let up to four players race on one screen, which made it a legendary multiplayer game. After that came Mario Kart Double Dash on the GameCube in two thousand three. The big idea was that each kart carried two characters, one driving and one throwing items. These games did not just repeat the first one. Each one added a clear new idea, and that is a big reason why the series has stayed interesting for so long, even when the basic rules did not change.

sections.heading: Handheld and Wii years
sections.script: Mario Kart did not stay on home consoles. Mario Kart DS arrived on the Nintendo DS in two thousand five and brought online racing to the series on a handheld. Then came Mario Kart Wii in two thousand eight, a game that came with a plastic steering wheel for the motion controls and made racing easy for anyone in the family to try. Mario Kart seven on the Nintendo three DS followed in two thousand eleven, adding gliders and underwater driving to the formula. These games show that the series was always willing to adapt to whatever new hardware Nintendo was making, using it to bring the same idea to more people in new ways.

sections.heading: Mario Kart 8 in twenty fourteen
sections.script: In twenty fourteen, Mario Kart eight launched on the Wii U on the twenty ninth of May in Japan and the thirtieth of May in North America and Europe. It introduced anti gravity sections, where karts drive on walls and ceilings, and it looked sharper and more colourful than any earlier entry. But the Wii U itself was not a big seller, so fewer people had the chance to play it, and that fact set the scene for what came next. Nintendo had a game that many fans loved on a console not many people owned, and the company decided that this was a game that deserved a second chance on its next system.

sections.heading: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe
sections.script: That second chance was Mario Kart Eight Deluxe, which came out on the Nintendo Switch on the twenty eighth of April, twenty seventeen. It included the Wii U game's tracks and add on content, along with new battle modes, and it quickly became a hit. Guinness World Records lists it as the best selling Mario video game, and news coverage reported that it passed sixty million copies in early twenty twenty four. GamingBolt reported a figure of sixty seven point three five million as of the end of December twenty twenty four. The game also got extra downloadable tracks over the years, so the same game kept getting fresh content far beyond its launch.

sections.heading: Mario Kart Tour and keeping the series alive
sections.script: Alongside the console games, Nintendo also made Mario Kart Tour, a game for mobile phones that appeared in twenty nineteen. It was built around short races that you could play with a touch screen, and it showed how the series could work on a different kind of device. Meanwhile, the Switch version of the main game continued to attract players year after year, helped by new tracks and by the fact that the series is easy to learn. Few racing series have lasted as long with such a steady identity, and fewer still have managed to stay so welcoming to brand new players at the same time. The karts change, the tracks change and the graphics improve, but the feeling of chaos on a final lap has stayed the same.

sections.heading: Mario Kart World on Switch 2
sections.script: Then came the next generation. Mario Kart World was announced in April twenty twenty five as a launch game for the Nintendo Switch two, and it was released worldwide on the fifth of June, twenty twenty five. The biggest change is size. Races now have twenty four racers, double the twelve that were in Mario Kart Wii, Mario Kart Eight and Mario Kart Eight Deluxe, and the tracks are connected in a large open world. It also introduced new modes, such as the Knockout Tour, where the field gets smaller at each checkpoint. After so many entries built around separate tracks and short cups, it was a real change of structure for the series, and it shows that Nintendo is still willing to rethink a formula that was already a huge success.

sections.heading: What makes Mario Kart work
sections.script: So why has Mario Kart lasted for so long? One reason is the items. Because the racers in the back get the strongest items, a beginner can still beat an expert on a lucky day, and that keeps everyone in the game. Another reason is that it is easy to explain: you only need to steer, accelerate and use an item. And the final reason is that it is made for playing together. Every game in the series, from the nineteen ninety two original to the newest one, invites friends to sit next to each other. That is something no other racing series has copied as well, and it explains why the name Mario Kart is known around the world.

sections.heading: Your favourite Mario Kart
sections.script: That was the history of Mario Kart, from Super Mario Kart in nineteen ninety two to Mario Kart World in twenty twenty five. Now it is your turn. Which Mario Kart game is your favourite, and which track do you love the most? Is it the classic Super Nintendo original, the Nintendo sixty four party nights, Mario Kart Wii, or the modern Eight Deluxe? And who is your go to racer? Share your answer in the comments below.
